Based on the supplied 2026 search results, I'd choose the **BLUETTI AC200L** because its built-in 30A TT-30 outlet makes it especially convenient for connecting an RV's shore-power cord. Dealectric reports a $854.05 discounted price using code `AFF5OFF`, although I haven't independently verified the checkout total. <Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="Source and RV comparison"/>

## How it compares

| Model | Reported price | Capacity | AC output | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | **$854.05 with code** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | RV shore-power connection |
| BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 | $899 | 2,074Wh | 2,600W | Battery longevity and output |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $899 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | Lightweight portability |
| ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 | $799 | 1,920Wh | 2,500W | Budget value |

Prices are from the supplied search results, not live checkout verification.

## Important RV considerations

- **30A outlet doesn't mean unlimited power.** The AC200L's 2,400W output corresponds to about 20A at 120V, despite its TT-30 connector.
- **Expect roughly 1.7–1.9kWh usable AC energy**, depending on inverter efficiency and load.
- **Air conditioning is challenging.** A typical RV rooftop A/C may exhaust a 2kWh battery in roughly 1–2 hours, assuming it can start and run within the station's power limits.
- **For extended off-grid camping**, solar charging or additional battery capacity matters more than a small difference in inverter wattage.

**Bottom line:** Buy the BLUETTI AC200L if the $854.05 discount is still available and you want a convenient RV connection. If you primarily power individual appliances rather than your RV's shore-power inlet, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 is also worth considering for its higher output and 6,000-cycle battery rating.
